meta.name: video-pipeline-blueprint design contract
meta.purpose: One machine-checked home for colour roles, type scale, spacing anchors, motion duties and text budgets.
meta.authority: Rank 1 source of truth. Components read src/design/tokens.ts, which is derived from this file.
meta.provenance: Rules distilled from ppt-master (hugohe3/ppt-master, MIT) design references - see docs/design-language.md for the item-by-item mapping.

palette.note: Colour is chosen by role, never by hex, and a preset is nothing more than a family that answers the same role names. That is why the gallery can render one layout in several looks without a single conditional in a scene: swap the family, keep the roles.

presets.note: Named looks. The default MUST stay the storyboard family: the 305 s film and the released stills were reviewed in it, so changing the default is a release, not a tweak. design_check.py validates every preset's contrasts with the same rules as any other family.

items.label: Midnight
items.note: The shipped look: near-black ground, warm paper text, coral accent. Frozen - this is what the reviewed film looks like.

items.label: Paper
items.note: Light, warm editorial page. Captions invert to dark text on a light scrim, so text.caption is a dark ink here rather than white.

items.label: Slate
items.note: Cool blue-black, colder than midnight, with a pale blue accent and an amber counter-accent. Same roles, different temperature.

lecture.note: The 305 s lecture and every showcase composition. Dark, low-luminance family; consecutive scenes stay inside it (K1).

storyboard.note: The generic storyboard template (src/storyboard). Deliberately a second, warmer family; values are frozen as shipped so existing template renders do not change. Merging it into one family is roadmap work, not a drive-by edit.

type.note: An ordered scale, not per-scene sizes. Roles pick a token; a new size is a contract change.

families.note: Named size sets for surfaces that are not the lecture's main ladder. Every value here is frozen from a render that was accepted, so an entry records what is on screen; it is not a recommendation for new work - new sizes come from 'scale'.

storyboard.note: The reusable template (Storyboard / Showreel). Freezing it turns D2 into a contract question: a scene names a role, not a pixel value.
trackingRules: CJK-bearing roles stay at or below 5% of the size; the subtitle was 6/44 = 13.6% until D3 was paid, and is now 2/44 = 4.5%
Latin-only overline may run wider (8/36 = 22.2%); design_check reports the ratio but does not fail on it. The ordinal is 2/30 = 6.7% and is not CJK-bearing

film.note: The multiplication film (2019 lines of new scene code). A third frozen family, because the lecture ladder stops at body 30 and this film needs roles between caption and display - a ladder, not advisory sizes.
trackingRules: label and meta are Latin/mono roles only (kickers, counters, the chapter bar); CJK text in this film carries zero tracking
3 px at 21 px = 14.3%, 2 px at 17 px = 11.8%, 8 px at 108 px = 7.4% and 1 px at 12 px = 8.3% are reported by design_check; all four are Latin, so none is a CJK deviation
cover (8 px on the HAWK wordmark) and micro (12 px vote-cell labels) were added for the Hawk paper film; additive keys only, no existing size changed

showcase.note: The HUD that sits under a showcase headline (chips, provenance rows, plate counters). These are labels at a fixed size next to a rendered image, not a ladder: freezing them keeps the design surface free of pixel literals without pretending 16/17/18/20/22 is a scale.
trackingRules: All five roles are Latin/mono only; the HUD carries no CJK at these sizes
3 px at 22 px = 13.6%, 2 px at 16 px = 12.5%, 1 px at 17 px = 5.9% - Latin, so design_check reports them as Latin and not as CJK deviations

ratchet.note: The 305 s lecture and the showcase samples keep their shipped sizes as an audited exception list, instead of growing this contract by forty ad-hoc tokens - freezing those would legitimise them as a scale.
ratchet.rule: A committed fontSize/letterSpacing literal is grandfathered. The only legal move is fewer literals: a new size means a token in 'scale' (or in a family) first, and a removed one must be deleted from the exception list in the same commit.

spacing.note: Layouts snap to these anchors so neighbouring scenes share rhythm. grid is the divisor everything else must be a multiple of.
rules: every anchor except cornerRadius is a multiple of grid

motion.note: Every animation declares a duty and takes its duration from that duty's budget. One dominant rhythm per scene; chrome never animates.

transition.why: cross-fades multiply two opacities and produce a dip no luma gate can see (K1)

static.meaning: no animation; the referent is already on screen

enter.meaning: element arrives after the scene is on screen

emphasize.meaning: a number or a block grows in importance

move.meaning: the same object changes place, not identity

ambient.meaning: slow drift that makes a static page breathe; must be slower than any duty above
ambient.rule: a scene shorter than minSeconds travels proportionally less rather than moving faster; past minSeconds the full kenBurns delta is reached, and a scene never exceeds maxSeconds of drift at the declared rate

text.note: Captions are derived from LINES, so these budgets are timing, not style.
text.rule: A sentence that needs more than maxCharsPerLine at the fast end of the range is two sentences, not a faster read.
